A_target.statement:
Let $s \in \R$ with $s > 1$.
Then:
:$\displaystyle \sum_{n \mathop = 1}^\infty \frac 1 {n^s} = \prod_p \frac 1 {1 - p^{-s} }$
where the product is over all primes.

B_source.statement: Every integer $n \ge 1$ is a product of primes in exactly one way, up to order.

substitutions.unique factorization: a bijection between integers and choices of prime exponents

derived.finite partial products: sums over integers with small prime factors

object_map.reformulation: Approximate the infinite product by finite products, each of which expands to a sum over integers with restricted prime factors.

validity_conditions: s > 1 is needed for absolute convergence of each geometric series and of the zeta series.
Finite products of absolutely convergent series may be multiplied out term by term.
proof_plan:
For each prime $p$, as $p^{-s} < 1$:
:$\displaystyle \frac 1 {1 - p^{-s} } = \sum_{k \mathop \ge 0} p^{-k s}$

For $N \ge 2$, multiplying finitely many absolutely convergent series:
:$\displaystyle \prod_{p \mathop \le N} \frac 1 {1 - p^{-s} } = \sum_{n \in S_N} \frac 1 {n^s}$
where $S_N$ is the set of $n$ whose prime factors are all at most $N$; by the source result each such $n$ appears exactly once.

As $S_N$ contains every $n \le N$:
:$\displaystyle 0 \le \sum_{n \mathop = 1}^\infty \frac 1 {n^s} - \prod_{p \mathop \le N} \frac 1 {1 - p^{-s} } \le \sum_{n \mathop > N} \frac 1 {n^s} \to 0$

Letting $N \to \infty$ gives the [[Euler Product Formula|Euler product]].
{{qed}}
